_comment: Every time window in the product, in one place, because the name
HISTORY_MONTHS had been used for four different quantities across two
languages: 60 in web/lib/request.ts (the basket window), 60 in
src/scenarios.py (a copy of it), 72 in src/inflation.py (how much CPI
to load) and 36 in src/precompute.py (what the weekly job fetched).
The last of those silently decided whether 850 funds had a 36-month
Read by src/windows.py and web/lib/windows.ts. Under web/ because the
frontend imports it directly and a Next build cannot reach outside its
tefas_reach_months is a measured fact, not a policy: on 2026-09-09,
asking tefas-crawler for 72, 84 and 120 months of GAL, AFO and TI2 all
returned the same first row, 2021-09-08. The floor is five years back
from today and it moves forward every day. This is why there is no
five-year return period: such a window would end at the last published
CPI month and would therefore need prices from before that floor.
return_periods_months is the single source for both the figures the
weekly job computes and the selector the fund page draws.
